jp-kanto-p1-cloudhq-asahi-deck.publisher: CloudHQ LLC (published by Inzai City as operator-provided council briefing material)
jp-kanto-p1-cloudhq-asahi-deck.summary: CloudHQ's deck on the full redevelopment of BIG HOP Garden Mall Inzai, titled Project Asahi (BIGHOPの全体再開発) Technology Campus. It introduces CloudHQ as a data-centre developer-operator whose first Japanese project is an Osaka joint venture with ESR, describes the mall's flat sales and rising costs, and states that 2025 investor marketing found no demand for a purely commercial redevelopment and interest only from data-centre-based parties. The Gensler site plan (page 31) shows two new 'DC' blocks with office space in the south-centre of the site, retail of 13,345 m2 by Inzai Makinohara Station, a 6,235 m2 community park, an 8,450 m2 non-DC future development plot, a larger future-development plot in the north, and 'EXISTING DCs' in the south-west corner. No capacity, floor area, schedule, permit or start of works is given for the data-centre blocks.
jp-kanto-p1-cloudhq-asahi-deck.title: CloudHQ: BIGHOPの全体再開発に関して (Project Asahi Technology Campus), Inzai City Council plenary briefing material of 29 September 2026

jp-kanto-p1-inzai-asahi-notice.summary: Inzai City reports that, while it revises the district plans of the three Hokuso Line station areas to make data-centre siting (zoning) explicit, the BIG HOP operator explained that it is planning a large-scale redevelopment of the ageing mall and is considering co-locating a data centre on the site and using the proceeds to rebuild the commercial facility. The city set up resident explanation sessions by the operator on 10 and 11 October 2026 and links the operator's material and the city's briefing, both presented at the 29 September 2026 council plenary briefing. The page's FAQ (first appearance not bounded; the page was edited after 29 September) adds that the operator plans two new data-centre buildings after first building the new commercial facilities and plazas, may consider further on-site buildings, targets operation around the mid-2030s with construction timing undecided, and that the plan is at an early stage with no prior consultation or permit procedure with the city.
